meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Quickly and without warning. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The boat suddenly hit a rock.

examples.text: Баржа внезапно наткнулась на что-то и стала тонуть.
examples.trans: The barge suddenly hit something and began to sink.

meanings.note: For emphasis. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').
Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

всякий.gloss: every kind of, all sorts of, any

meanings.en: all sorts of, every kind of
meanings.note: всякое бывает = all sorts of things happen
На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'який').

examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen.
Take an umbrella just in case.

examples.text: Ладно, всякое бывает. Ну что вы?
examples.trans: Alright, all sorts of things happen. Oh, come on.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we will finish talking'.

examples.text: Тихо, мы с тобой потом договорим.
examples.trans: Quiet, you and I will finish talking later.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и договорить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will finish talking on time.

related.gloss: to we will finish talking (prefixed perfective)
not to we will finish talking (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose. Core Russian adv meaning 'what for, why' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: In one direction, now. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.
To run for a second term. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (on foot)', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.

examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'make, cause'.

examples.text: Что, я зря пришла? Я надела костюм зайки!
examples.trans: What, did I come for nothing? I put on a bunny costume!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'резать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to slice', forming an aspectual pair with 'нарезать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to carve') (to slice meat or bread) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вот теперь кусочки нарезаны красиво и аккуратно.
examples.trans: Now the pieces are cut beautifully and neatly.

examples.text: Сначала мелко нарежь лук и морковь.
examples.trans: First chop the onion and carrot finely.
I will cut the vegetables into even pieces.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'the heck, away (colloq.)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Why on earth did you do that to us.

examples.text: На кухне все стараются работать нафиг.
examples.trans: In the kitchen everyone tries to work the heck.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'много'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to do a bit of work.

examples.text: Мы даём вам ещё немного времени.
examples.trans: We are giving you a little more time.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: end-stressed in all oblique forms: ножа, ножом

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
There is a sharp knife on the table.

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

meanings.note: Поставить защёлку = fit a latch. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to put, to place (upright)', paired with 'ставить'.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'fool'.

examples.text: Вокруг меня одни лентяи и придурки!
examples.trans: Around me are only slackers and fools!

examples.text: Ну ты и придурок, честное слово!
examples.trans: Well you are a jerk, honestly!

припугнуть.gloss: to scare a little, to give a fright

meanings.en: to give a scare, to frighten a bit
meanings.note: Colloquial; при- adds 'a little'. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'пугнуть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to scare a little, to give a fright', paired with 'пугать'.

examples.text: Мы так его припугнём, и всё.
examples.trans: We'll just give him a scare, that's all.
He only wanted to scare his neighbour a bit.

examples.text: Кто тебя заставляет пытать, Самсон? Мы так его припугнём, и всё.
examples.trans: Who is making you torture anyone, Samson? We'll just give him a scare, that's all.

meanings.en: to happen, take place, go on
meanings.note: Что происходит? = What is going on?

examples.trans: What is going on? I don't understand.

examples.text: Мы не знаем, что с нашей дочерью происходит!
examples.trans: We don't know what is happening with our daughter!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: informal: a group of young men; ребята! = guys!
Colloquial plural of ребёнок. Common substantive noun meaning 'guys, lads, kids (plural only)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The boys will have a word with you.

examples.text: Тогда ребята с тобой поработают. До свидания, Аркадий Борисович.
examples.trans: Then the boys will have a little word with you. Goodbye, Arkady Borisovich.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

На всякий случай = just in case. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучай'). Common masculine noun meaning 'case, occasion, incident' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Возьмите, пожалуйста. На случай, если передумаете.
examples.trans: Please take this. In case you change your mind.

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!
Не трогай! = Don't touch!. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to touch', paired with 'тронуть'.

examples.text: Всё, хорошо, я тебя выпущу! Только собаку не трогай!
examples.trans: All right, fine, I'll let you out! Just don't touch the dog!
